contexts.text: The third style of the Word is the prophetic, which was born from the style of the Most Ancient Church. But it is not continuous... and is scarcely intelligible except in the internal sense, where are the greatest arcana, which follow in a beautiful connected order, and regard the external and the internal man, many states of the Church, Heaven itself, and, in the inmosts, the Lord. AC 1139. SE 2721.
(The prophetic style was to prevent profanation.)
Prophets = those who teach. AC 1460:2.
Representatives like those seen by the prophets. AC 1532.
A prophet = one who teaches, thus the doctrine of Knowledges.
The visions of the prophets were nothing else than openings of their interior sight. Example(s). AC 1619. AC 4527:end.
When moved by the prophetic Spirit...
Visions were different to Moses from what they were to the prophets. Explained.
This is especially the case with the prophetic Word of the Old Testament.
There were Angels who... spoke through the prophets. AC 1925:4, Explained.
On prophetic visions and dreams. General article. AC 1970. AC 1975. AC 1976. AC 2179:2. AC 2179:3.
The duplex expressions in the prophets. Explained.
That there is an internal sense in the propheticals may be believed more easily...
Prophets. here, = those who teach falsities. AC 3301:2.
Because he is a prophet () = that thus it would be taught.

A prophet, in the sense of the letter, = those to whom there is revelation; and also, abstractedly, the revelation itself: but in the internal sense, one who teaches; and also, abstractedly, the doctrine itself. And as the Lord is doctrine itself, or the Word which teaches, He is called a prophet. Illustrated.
To prophesy = to teach. AC 2567:5.
Came ye out to see a prophet? I say... more than a prophet (). A prophet = the externals of doctrine and worship.
(Delight of a heathen) when I read to him something from the propheticals.
The prophetical Books enumerated.
(Prophetical parts where there is no sense in the letter.)
The prophetical writings in the Ancient Church. AC 2897, Explained. AC 2898.
Where, in the prophets, good is spoken of, so also is truth.
False prophets () = those who teach truths not Divine, or falsities.
Sons of the prophets = those who teach.

Spoken of by Daniel the prophet = by the prophets; for when any prophet is mentioned in the Word by name, it is the prophetic Word itself which is meant... By Daniel is meant all the prophetic concerning the Lord's Advent, and the state of the Church.

Vastation is much treated of in the prophets, and by it in the sense of the letter is signified the vastation of the Jewish and Israelitish Church; but, in the internal sense, the vastation of the Church in general; thus that which is now at hand. TCR 758.
The sun shall go down upon the prophets () = that they will no longer have truth and the doctrine of truth. Prophets = those who teach the truths of doctrine.
(This) was from the proprium of the prophet.
To hear Moses and the prophets = to know the things in the Word, and to have faith in it; thus also to will them.
There shall arise false Christs and false prophets = the falsities of that doctrine.
(Thus) the Spirit spoke with the prophets not as a man with a man, but as a spirit with a man, that is, in him. Illustrated.
The prophets were clad in coats of hair, because by the prophets was represented the Lord as to the truths of doctrine...

Hence, by the prophets, in the Word, to whom truth Divine was manifested either by speech, by visions, or by dreams, are signified those who teach truths; and, in the abstract sense, the truths of doctrine.
To prophesy = to teach and preach them. AC 4682:3.
The form in which He appeared to the prophets.

Such were most of the revelations of the prophets in the Jewish Church: they heard a voice, they saw a vision, or they dreamed a dream; but, as they had no perception, they were merely verbal or visual revelations...
Priests = goods; prophets, those who teach.

It is known from the Word that there was an influx from the World of Spirits and from Heaven into the prophets, partly by dreams, partly by visions, and partly by speech; and also, with some, into the speech itself, and into the gestures themselves; thus into the things which are of the body; and that they then did not speak from themselves, or act from themselves, but from the Spirits who then occupied their bodies. Example(s).

(Thus) was I instructed how the prophets, through whom Spirits spoke and acted, were possessed; namely, that the Spirits occupied their bodies, insomuch that scarcely anything was left except that they knew that they existed. There were certain Spirits for this use, who did not want to obsess men, but only to enter into the corporeal affections of the man; and, when they entered into these, they entered into all things of the body... The Spirits who possessed my body, as formerly the bodies of the prophets, said that at the time they knew no otherwise than that they had life as in the body.

There were also other influxes with the prophets; namely, that they exercised their own discretion and thought, only that the spirits were speaking with them, for the most part inwardly in them; the influx not being into the thought and will, but merely discourse which came to their hearing.

The reason the Word is prophetical, is that when it is read it is not understood by the man except obscurely; and when it is understood obscurely by such a man as there is now, it is perceived by the Angels clearly.
The Law and the prophets = the Word in each and all things.
Elias represents the Lord as to the prophets...

The prophets wrote as the Spirit from the Divine dictated; for the very words which they wrote were uttered in their ears. With them was the truth which proceeds mediately from the Divine, that is, through Heaven, but not the truth which proceeds immediately; for they had not a perception of what each thing signified.

Hence Aaron is here called Moses' prophet... that is, one who utters adequately to the understanding the Divine truth which proceeds immediately from the Lord, and which transcends all understanding. And, as a prophet is one who teaches and utters Divine truth adequately to the understanding, a prophet = the doctrine of the Church. AC 7269, Explained. AR 8:5.
The prophets who see vanity and divine a lie () = those who teach evils and falsities. AC 9248.
Miriam the prophetess (). Explained.
The prophets = doctrines from the Word.
The Word in the letter, especially the prophetic one, is nothing else (than the density of a cloud) relatively to the internal sense.
Prophets and apostles () = the truths and goods of the Church.
That prophet () is the Lord. Illustrated.
A prophet = one who teaches; in the abstract sense, doctrine; thus the Lord as to the Word or Divine truth.

No prophet is accepted in his own country () = that the Lord and the Divine truth from Him are less received and loved at heart within the Church than outside it... A prophet, in this sense, = the Lord as to the Divine truth, thus as to the doctrine of the Church.
Prophets = the doctrine of truth which is through the Word from the Lord.
Prophets = those who teach the truths and goods of faith; and, in the abstract sense, the doctrines of faith. Illustrated.
That the prophetic Word would perish. Representation.
More than a prophet = that the Word is more than any doctrine in the world.
That all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John. Explained.
Such things appeared also to the prophets, when their interior sight was opened. Illustrated.
The Lord is called a prophet when truth is treated of.
Prophets (in the series kings, princes, priests, and prophets) = doctrines.
The prophets are called holy because by them is signified the Word, which is the Divine truth; and, in special, doctrines from the Word.
The reason the prophets were anointed, was that the prophets represented the Lord as to the doctrine of Divine truth, consequently as to the Word. AE 375:15.
A disciple = the truth of life; a prophet, the truth of doctrine.

How the Lord spoke with the prophets. - Not by an influx into their interiors, but through Spirits who were sent to them, whom the Lord filled with His aspect, and thus inspired the words which they dictated to the prophets... As the words came forth immediately from the Lord, each of them is filled with what is Divine, and contains in itself an internal sense... A Spirit who is filled with the Divine knows not but that he is the Lord...
The Mohammedans who had acknowledged the Lord as the Greatest Prophet...
Prophets = those who teach truth, and through it lead to good; and false prophets, those who teach falsity, and by it seduce.
The prophets represented the Lord as to the Word, and thence as to the Church; and the Lord was the Prophet. Illustrated.
By the Lord as the greatest prophet, is signified the Church itself and the Word itself. DLord 16:5, Illustrated.

The prophets were called sons of man because they represented the Lord as to the Word, and thence signified the doctrine of the Church from the Word... For the spiritual signification of a prophet is the doctrine of the Church from the Word; and, when said of the Lord, the Word itself. Illustrated. DSS 35.
That Jehovah Himself... spoke the Word through the prophets. Explained.

When the prophets were in vision, they were not in their bodies, but in their spirits, in which state they saw such things as are in Heaven. But when Jehovah spoke with them, they were in their bodies, and heard Jehovah speaking. These two states of the prophets are to be carefully distinguished. Explained, Illustrated. AR 36. AR 945:2.
It is not said in the prophets that they spoke the Word from the Holy Spirit, but that they spoke it from Jehovah... Illustrated. AR 36:end. TCR 158.
By the name, and the reward, of a prophet, is meant the state and happiness of those who are in Divine truths.

The words of this prophecy () = the doctrine of the New Jerusalem; for by a prophet, in the abstract sense, is signified the doctrine of the Church from the Word; thus, here, the doctrine of the New Church; and the like by a prophecy.

The reason prophet and prophecy = the doctrine of the Church from the Word, is that the Word was written through the prophets... and therefore when a prophet is mentioned, since his function was to write and teach the Word, there is meant the Word as to doctrine, or doctrine from the Word. Hence the Lord, being the Word itself, was called the prophet.
That by a prophet is meant the doctrine of the Church from the Word. Illustrated.
To receive a prophet in the name of a prophet = to receive the doctrine of truth because it is true. AE 102:6.
Prophets and priests = the universal Church as to the truth of doctrine and the good of life. Illustrated.
The Word was not revealed in a state of vision, but was dictated by the Lord to the prophets viva voce. And therefore it is nowhere said that they spoke from the Holy Spirit, but from Jehovah.
To kill the prophets () = to destroy the truths of doctrine from the Word.

Who calleth herself a prophetess () = who make it the doctrine itself of the Church, and found all their theology upon it. By a prophet, in the Word, is signified the doctrine of the Church; in like manner therefore by a prophetess. ( = the doctrine of all falsities. AE 160.)
The prophets and apostles are called holy because by prophets and apostles are signified the truths of doctrine of the Church.
By the mystery of God evangelized to the prophets () is signified that which has been foretold by the Lord in the Word, and has hitherto been hidden.
Thou must prophesy again... () = that they must be further taught.
Those two prophets tormented them... () = that these two essentials... are in opposition...
To give reward to His servants the prophets... () = the happiness of eternal life to those who are in truths of doctrine from the Word...
The blood of saints and prophets have they poured out () = that (faith alone) when received, perverts all true doctrinals from the Word.
Ye holy apostles and prophets () = the men of the Church who are in goods and truths from the Word... Prophets = truths from good from the Word.

In her was found the blood of prophets and of saints () = the adulteration and profanation of every truth of the Word and of the Church... Prophets = all who are in Divine truths from the Word; and, abstractedly, the truths of doctrine from the Word.
The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy () = that it is the all of the Word and of the doctrine thence.

The Lord God of the holy prophets () = the Lord from whom is the Word of both Covenants; for by prophets are signified those who teach truths from the Word; and, in the abstract sense, the doctrine of truth of the Church; and, in a wide sense, the Word itself, (thus) the Word of both Covenants.
Blessed is he that keepeth the words of this prophecy () = that the Lord will give eternal life to those who keep and do the truths or precepts of the doctrine of this Book, now opened by the Lord.
I am... of thy brethren the prophets () = those who are in the doctrine of the New Jerusalem.
Seal not the words of this prophecy () = that the Apocalypse is not to be closed up.
Everyone that heareth the words of the prophecy of this Book () = those who read and know the truths of doctrine of this Book now opened by the Lord. AR 958.
The last temptation which the Lord as the Grand Prophet sustained. TCR 129, Explained.
That the prophets represented the state of their Church as to doctrine from the Word, and as to life according to it. Illustrated.
The Spirit of prophecy = the truth of doctrine from the Word; for prophecy = nothing else than doctrine; and to prophesy = to teach it. ( = the life and soul of doctrine. AE 10:2.)

As in a state of the mind separated from the body, the prophets saw such things as come forth in the Spiritual World, it is called a vision of God... This is the state in which I have been for twenty-six years, with the difference that I have been in the spirit and body at the same time, and only sometimes out of the body. Illustrated.
The Law and the prophets = the whole Word.
The New Church as treated of in the prophets. Illustrated.
On the speech of Spirits with Moses and the prophets. Explained.

The prophetic spirit in the representative Church, which was given to whomsoever the Lord pleased, thus to the seventy elders who prophesied by the spirit of Moses. Thus did Saul prophesy. Which prophetic Spirit was nothing else than that they spoke and acted under words and ways that were unknown to them... SE 2282.
On the action of Spirits into the prophets (in causing them to assume various postures). Explained.
In like manner were the old prophets obsessed. (Explained.)

External men were actuated by such a prophetic spirit as that of Saul... But interior men... if possessed by a like spirit, are left to themselves, both as to the thoughts and the acts; and therefore it was foretold that prophecies should cease, namely, through the Lord...
Other prophetic influxes. Explained.
If they should read the prophetic Books without the points...
The prophetic writings, where the sense is understood by no one except the Lord...
On certain troops of prophets in the Old Testament.
Under Paul, see this reference.
On the two prophets in .
That not the Holy Spirit, but an Angel, spoke to the prophets. Explained.
Hence it is that all things the Angels said to the prophets were Divine, and not at all from the Angels. Explained.
The words of this prophecy = the truths which are of the doctrine of Heaven.
Under Apostle, see this reference.
Prophets = those who teach truths. AE 141:8. AE 152:4. AE 329:25.
By all the prophets are signified the doctrines of Divine truth.
A prophet = one who teaches truth; and, in the abstract sense, the doctrine of truth. AE 235:7. AE 653:10. AE 706:3. AE 710:12. AE 866:5. AE 975. AE 1193.
Prophets = the truths of doctrine. AE 433:33. AE 537:17. AE 655:9. AE 659:23.
Prophets = doctrines. AE 237:3. AE 240:3.
Prophets = those in the truths of doctrine; and, abstractedly, the truths of doctrine. AE 376:32. AE 376:34. AE 386:7. AE 395:3. AE 419:16.
The priest and the prophet = the doctrine of good and truth.
The blood of the prophets = the falsification of the truths of doctrine.
Prophets, in the Word, = the doctrine of Divine truth; thus the Divine truth as to doctrine.
Prophets = false doctrines.
A prophet = the doctrine of truth, and thence the knowledge of truth; but here the doctrine and knowledge of falsity.
A prophet = doctrine from the Word.
Prophets = those who teach truths, and the intelligent; and, abstractedly, the doctrine of truth, and intelligence.
A prophet = one who teaches truths; and, in the abstract sense, the doctrine of genuine truth which is from the Lord. AE 600:20.
The incantations in which the prophets were skilled. Explained.
His servants the prophets () = those who are in the truths of doctrine, and receive.
His servants the prophets () = the truths of doctrine, here, the Word.
The prophet John.

The reason to prophesy = to teach the Word, is that by a prophet, in the supreme sense, is meant the Lord as to the Word; and, in the relative sense, one who teaches the Word; but, in the abstract sense, the Word itself, and also doctrine from the Word. Hence, to prophesy = to teach the Word and also to teach doctrine from the Word. Fully illustrated.

By prophets, in the spiritual sense, are meant all whom the Lord leads, and with whom also the Lord inflows, and reveals to them the arcana of the Word, whether they teach them, or not. AE 624:15. AE 624:16, Illustrated.

The prophets of the Old Testament were not illustrated as to the understanding; but only received in the hearing the words which they were to say or write, without understanding their interior and still less their spiritual sense.
In the opposite sense, by prophets are signified perversions and falsifications of the Word, and falsities of doctrine. Illustrated.
To kill the prophets = to extinguish Divine truth by the falsification of the Word.
In a word, prophets teach; and priests lead.
So persecuted they the prophets who were before you = that formerly they had in like manner assaulted the truths of doctrine.
The judge and the prophet = the doctrine of good and of truth.
All the prophets represented the Church as to doctrine from the Word.
By a prophet, in general, is signified the doctrine of the Church from the Word.

Therefore, when the eyes of the spirit were opened with the prophets, they saw such things as represented the Divine celestial and Divine spiritual things of the Church; and also such things as represented the future things which would happen in the Churches.
Each of the chapters in the prophetic Word corresponds to one of the Societies of Heaven. (Continued. See Prophets and Psalms (the work).)
